blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Global supply chain strategy at senior level is about deciding, deliberately, which geographies you depend on, which you merely trade with, and which you treat as pure opportunity. Those three categories need different structures, different governance, and different amounts of attention. Treating them all the same is the classic mistake — it concentrates risk quietly and erodes the company's ability to respond when a specific region turns difficult.

At this level, the useful frame is not cost alone. It is cost versus concentration versus resilience versus access. A dependence on one country for a critical input is cheap until the political weather changes. A diversified supplier base is more expensive until a single region becomes impossible. The right answer depends on the company's strategic tolerance for surprise — and on honest conversations about what the board would regret most if things went wrong in the worst year.

Good global strategy is uncomfortable, because it forces explicit choices nobody wants to make in good times. The companies that make them anyway tend to be the ones still standing when the good times end.

items.q: According to the text, what is the "classic mistake" in global supply chain strategy?
options: Treating all three categories of geography the same way
Trading only with politically stable countries
items.why: "Treating them all the same is the classic mistake — it concentrates risk quietly."

items.q: Which frame does the author say is genuinely useful at senior level?
options: Cost versus concentration versus resilience versus access
items.why: "the useful frame is not cost alone. It is cost versus concentration versus resilience versus access."

items.q: What does "cheap until the political weather changes" most strongly IMPLY?
options: Cost should never influence sourcing decisions
Cheap suppliers are always politically unstable
Weather forecasting improves supply chain planning
Political risk makes concentration expensive only in hindsight
items.why: Inferência: a economia da dependência é ilusória — o preço real só aparece quando a região vira problema.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Resilience is worth paying for against a bad year.
Explicit trade-offs are easier to avoid when times are good.
Diversification carries a real cost in normal conditions.
The lowest-cost sourcing option is always the wisest choice.
items.why: Inferência: o texto inteiro argumenta que custo sozinho não é o critério — a dependência barata esconde risco.

items.q: What does the final sentence suggest about companies that make uncomfortable choices?
options: They tend to survive when conditions deteriorate
They grow faster than their rivals in good times
They rarely need a governance framework
items.why: "tend to be the ones still standing when the good times end" — resistem quando o ciclo vira.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James apresentando ao comitê a conclusão da revisão de cadeia de suprimentos. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, after three months, here is where the review lands — and I won't pretend it's comfortable. We are recommending that our dependence on that single region drops from eighty per cent of the critical input to fifty-five. That is a deliberate, expensive choice, and I want to own it clearly rather than dress it up.

Let me be honest about how we got here. Had we built a second origin two years ago, when a few of us argued for it, this correction would have been gradual and cheap. We didn't, so it's now abrupt and it will cost margin in the first year. I'm not raising that to reopen old arguments — only so we don't make the same call again.

The number itself, fifty-five, isn't sacred. What matters is the principle behind it: no single geography should be able to hold the whole book hostage. We stress-tested the position against three disruption scenarios, and in the worst of them, the current setup was simply indefensible.

I'd rather this board regret paying for resilience we didn't strictly need than regret the year we couldn't ship at all.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What specific change is James recommending?
options: Building three new origins within the year
Cutting costs across every region by fifty-five per cent
Increasing dependence on the cheapest region
Reducing dependence on one region from 80% to 55% of the critical input
items.why: "our dependence on that single region drops from eighty per cent of the critical input to fifty-five."

items.q: Why does James say the correction is now "abrupt" and costly?
options: Because the region has already become impossible to use
Because a second origin was not built two years ago
Because the board rejected the review
items.why: "Had we built a second origin two years ago… this correction would have been gradual and cheap. We didn't."

items.q: What does James mean by "no single geography should be able to hold the whole book hostage"?
options: The book should be closed during disruptions
The company should stop trading globally
One region should never control the entire position by itself
Every region should hold an equal share
items.why: Inferência: o princípio é evitar que uma única origem tenha poder de reféns sobre toda a operação.

items.q: What can be inferred about the specific figure of fifty-five per cent?
options: It was chosen to minimise cost
It is a legally required threshold
It is the maximum the board would approve
It matters less than the principle it protects
items.why: Inferência: "The number itself… isn't sacred. What matters is the principle behind it."

items.q: How would you best describe James's final position?
options: He believes cost should decide the outcome
He prefers regretting unused resilience over a year of not shipping
He wants to reopen the old sourcing arguments
He is confident the disruption will never happen
items.why: "I'd rather this board regret paying for resilience we didn't strictly need than regret the year we couldn't ship at all."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Quiet dependence erodes the company's ability to respond." To erode means to…
items.why: Erode = erodir, desgastar aos poucos — aqui, a capacidade de resposta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The three categories each need different structures and different ___."
items.why: Governance = governança: como cada categoria é dirigida e controlada.

items.q: "The board must define its tolerance for surprise." This refers to…
options: how much unexpected risk the company is willing to absorb
how quickly the company reacts to news
the number of scenarios it can model
items.why: Tolerância à surpresa: quanto de imprevisto a empresa aceita carregar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Geographic ___ looks efficient until a disruption reveals its fragility."
items.why: Concentração de risco parece eficiente, mas expõe fragilidade numa ruptura.

items.q: "A diversified base builds resilience against a bad year." Resilience is…
options: the capacity to withstand and recover from shocks
items.why: Resiliência = capacidade de resistir a choques e se recuperar deles.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem numa revisão de estratégia global. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee still has to sign off on the new sourcing split." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the second origin over four quarters." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, por etapas.

items.q: "Procurement pushed back on the diversification target." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The plan was agreed two years ago, but nobody followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Trimming one point of cost won't move the needle on our exposure." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
